citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed rest), occipital channels O1 and Oz, first 10 s (1600 samples) at 160 Hz -- the SAME git-tracked pair the sibling PLV case (eeg-plv-alpha-eegmmidb) uses.
pipeline: readRDS(o1_s002r02) + readRDS(oz_s002r02) -> PhysioCrossModal::phaseLagIndex(freq_band=c(8,13)): band-pass (Butterworth order 4) both channels to alpha, take the Hilbert instantaneous phase, and compute PLI = |mean(sign(sin(phi_O1 - phi_Oz)))|. The reference re-computes the PLI with an independent scipy pipeline (butter+filtfilt+hilbert), checks the sign formula, and recovers ground truth on constructed zero-lag / lagged / independent signals (via reticulate). Deterministic (the contrast is seeded).
note: The tracked inputs are eval/data/plv-eeg/{o1,oz}_s002r02.rds. The phase-lag index (Stam 2007) is the volume-conduction-robust phase-connectivity measure: it counts only CONSISTENT non-zero phase lags, so it is ~0 for zero-lag coupling (volume conduction / common reference). phaseLagIndex is validated three ways: the sign formula is exact; it reproduces an independent scipy Hilbert-band PLI to ~4e-3 (an agreement -- beyond the filtfilt convention, PLI's sign() is more sensitive near zero-lag); and it recovers ground truth with the diagnostic contrast (constructed zero-lag -> PLV 0.99 but PLI 0.01; lagged -> PLI 1.0; independent -> both ~0). The finding: on the real O1-Oz pair whose alpha PLV is 0.92, the PLI is only 0.016 -- the strong occipital alpha 'synchronization' is dominated by near-zero-lag coupling (volume conduction / common reference), the textbook reason PLI/wPLI are preferred over PLV. (PLI is conservative and can miss genuine near-zero-lag interactions; this is a methodological demonstration, not a claim of no coupling.)
